paragraphs: Rabbi Yonatan bar Yosef: Berakhot 22a, ‘Rabbi Yose says,’ and so forth; ‘Rabbi Yonatan ben Yosef says,’ and so forth; ‘Rabbi Natan ben Avshalom says,’ and so forth; ‘Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar, Rabbi Akiva’s student, says,’ and so forth; ‘Rabbi Yehudah says.’ Avot, chapter 4: ‘Anyone who fulfills the Torah in poverty,’ and so forth. Rosh Hashanah 13a, end: ‘As it was taught, Rabbi Yonatan ben Yosef says,’ and so forth. Niddah 85b, beginning: he disputes with Rabbi Yose be-Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya; Yoma 85b. In some places: Rabbi Natan ben Yosef. Tosefta, Terumot, chapter 8, and Kelim, Bava Metzia, chapter 3. Berakhot 47b: ‘Rabbi Eliezer says; Rabbi Yehoshua says; Ben Azzai says; Rabbi Natan says,’ and so forth; ‘Rabbi Natan bar Yosef says; Others say.’ Megillah 31b: ‘Others say,’ and so forth; ‘Rabbi Natan bar Yosef says,’ and so forth; ‘Some say,’ and so forth. Also Ketubbot 60b, Niddah 61b, and Avot de-Rabbi Natan, beginnings of chapters 29 and 30. Certainly all are one. Chullin 139a, ‘Rabbi Yochanan bar Yosef,’ is also a scribal error. Yuchasin forgot to include him in alphabetical order, but included him at the end of the sequence of generations. He writes: ‘I was uncertain whether he was a priest. Since he was a tanna, he was Rabbi Yoshiyah’s colleague in the baraita and Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani’s teacher; see his entry. Rabbi Yoshiyah, Rabbi Yonatan’s colleague, lived in Rabbi Elazar’s days; see his entry. Therefore Maimonides placed him at the end of the tannaim. The doubt about his priesthood is because Bava Metzia 90b has Rabbi Yonatan asking Rabbi Simai about muzzling a cow, and so forth. He replied: “You learn from your father’s house: wine and strong drink,” and so forth. Rashi explains that he was a priest. But Berakhot 18a has Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Yonatan walking in a cemetery; see his entry. In Sanhedrin 71 he said: “I sat upon the grave of the stubborn and rebellious son”; see Rabbi Shimon ben Yose ben Lakonya. It appears he was not a priest. It appears that this is Rabbi Yonatan, Rabbi Yoshiyah’s colleague, since he was at the end of the tannaim and Rabbi Chiyya lived in his time: both lived in Rabbi’s days, and he disputes with Rabbi Yoshiyah. The other Rabbi Yonatan was a priest. In Chullin 70b Rabbi Yonatan spoke with Ben Azzai, and in Sifra, Behar. Perhaps this is the one mentioned in Avot, chapter 4.’ End quotation. This requires examination: wherever Rabbi Yonatan and his colleague Rabbi Yoshiyah are mentioned, he is not called Rabbi Yonatan ben Yosef, but simply Rabbi Yonatan. Why does Yuchasin bring this here under Rabbi Yonatan ben Yosef? It is true that the unqualified Rabbi Yonatan and his colleague Rabbi Yoshiyah lived in an early period, for they were Rabbi Yishmael’s students; see his entry. The unqualified Rabbi Yonatan spoke with Shimon ben Azzai; Rabbi Yonatan ben Yosef was likewise among the early ones, as you see above from those with whom he disputed, and he also disputes with Ben Azzai. Rabbi Yoshiyah, Rabbi Yonatan’s colleague, lived long, until Rabbi Elazar’s days—that is, ben Pedat; see his entry. We find Rabbi Yonatan with Rabbi Chiyya; see his entry and above. Thus Rabbi Yonatan, Rabbi Yoshiyah’s colleague, also lived long, being Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani’s teacher.
